text:
The Seattle City Council convened to discuss Agenda Item 14, a bill recommended by the Public Safety, Civil Rights and Technology Committee to amend employment ordinances in Seattle. The legislation aims to strengthen labor laws, protect workers, penalize bad actors, and provide clarity to businesses regarding their rights and responsibilities. Councilmember Harrell introduced the bill, noting it originated from a "green sheet" request to the Mayor’s office to increase penalties for labor law violations and clarify worker remedies. The Office of Labor Standards engaged stakeholders in approximately 26 meetings to develop the 175-page bill.

Key provisions include a private right of action for paid, sick, and safe time, minimum wage, and wage theft remedies, allowing employees to seek legal and equitable relief up to three times unpaid wages. Penalties for retaliation are set at up to $5,000, with attorney’s fees and costs covered. The effective date is April 1, 2016, for businesses with 50 or more employees, and April 1, 2017, for smaller businesses, allowing time for education and acclimation. The bill also increases remedies for violations of the Fair Chance Employment Ordinance, with penalties escalating from $500 for first violations to $5,000 for third violations. Civil penalties for wage theft and other violations range from $500 to $5,000 per aggrieved party, depending on the severity and recurrence of the violation.

The legislation emphasizes a methodology designed to encourage investigation, education, and settlement, while granting the Office of Labor Standards discretion to enforce aggressively. A six-month check-in is scheduled to assess the effectiveness of the new remedies. Councilmember Licata highlighted the importance of effective enforcement mechanisms, while Councilmember Swan noted the prevalence of wage theft and the need for stronger deterrents. Both expressed support for the bill, emphasizing its impact on workers and the necessity of unionization and worker education.

The Council voted to pass the bill, with eight in favor and one opposed. Following the passage, the meeting moved to Agenda Items 15 and 16, concerning the re-appointment of Tara Henriksen to the Seattle Fire Advisory Board and James B. Moran to the Fire Code Advisory Board.
